blocks.md: **Between 1996 and 2018 Brazil raised its real minimum wage by 128%. Over the same years earnings inequality among men aged 18–54 fell steeply: the standard deviation of log earnings went from ≈ 0.86 to ≈ 0.67 (chart-read), and its correlation with the real minimum wage is −0.973. The decline was concentrated at the bottom (P50/P10) and in low-income states, where the minimum bites hardest.**

sections.heading: National distribution relative to the minimum

blocks.src: assets/Attachments/Engbom and Moser 2022 - Brazil wage distributions and percentile ratios.png
blocks.alt: Engbom and Moser 2022 - Brazil wage distributions and percentile ratios

blocks.md: In 1996 the distribution of log earnings (in multiples of the minimum) is wide; by 2018 it is compressed and bunched just above the minimum. Normalized to 1 in 1996, the log P50/P10 ratio falls to ≈ 0.62 by 2018 and the log P90/P50 ratio only to ≈ 0.85 (chart-read).

blocks.src: assets/Attachments/Engbom and Moser 2022 - inequality in high- and low-income Brazilian states.png
blocks.alt: Engbom and Moser 2022 - inequality in high- and low-income Brazilian states

blocks.md: The three lowest-income states (Maranhão, Piauí, Paraíba) saw the variance of log wages and lower-tail ratios fall far more than the three highest-income (Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo, Distrito Federal): the same national minimum bites more where wages are low. This is the variation Lee's and Autor, Manning and Smith's approach exploits.

blocks.src: assets/Attachments/Engbom and Moser 2022 - minimum wage effects by percentile.png
blocks.alt: Engbom and Moser 2022 - minimum wage effects by percentile

blocks.md: Regressions in the style of Lee and AMS (state fixed effects and trends, OLS; IV similar) give marginal effects on the log wage gap relative to the median of ≈ 0.55 at the 10th percentile, declining to 0 near the median and slightly negative above it; relative to the 90th percentile, effects stay positive up to about the 80th percentile — spillovers further up than in the US (chart-read).
